questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The renomé of Universidad de Complutense combined with inspiration from other Erasmus students who have studied in Madrid

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Rather easy, given the size of Universidad Complutense it has been my experience that the inprocessing of new students works very well

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There has been 2 in-processing events held at the university upon arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It can be challenging to find housing in Madrid. Especially if the budget is tight- which seems to be the case for almost every student. I would recommend using the sit "idealista" but with the caveat to only reach out to private landlords avoiding companies.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should know, that if you study at the Ciudad Universitaria Campus, then the areas Chamberí, Arguëlles, Arapiles, Sol, Lavapies, Malasaña are all nice areas to live.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process consist of two inprocessing events where you recieve relevant information. Afterwards students attend the Erasmus office where the Proof of Attendance is signed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus office has been both helpful and available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I managed to get all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At Complutense the two first weeks of the semester is an opportunity to try out different classes. Take advantage of these two weeks although it may challenge some of the deadlines at your sending university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the classes has been high and requires a working knowledge both in spanish and preferably also a sound background knowledge of the subject matter i.e. literature, linguistics etc. Future students should consider how many different masters they take classes from as choosing courses from various masters may challenge both the social aspects as well as the students ability to cope with different teaching styles.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching at Complutense is more unilateral and the distance between teacher and students seem further.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A broad range: from theater to football, Rugby, Padel, swimming and more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any activiyt where you find like-minded people. I have heard that salsa classes have been a great succes for some students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the movies and focus to explore Madrid instead of traveling far. There is plenty of opportunities to explore in the city of Madrid.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Spanish people are quite easy to connect with.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Invite your classmates for coffee or "cañas" after class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It has not been my experience that the cultural differences between Denmark and Spain are hard to gap.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and the fact that Complutense students are very inclusive.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
(1) Make sure to take courses where you like the teachers. It is a good idea to do some research on the teachers. Some of them participate in podcasts or can be found on youtube where they give or participate in academic presentations.

(2) Try to limit yourself to ideally 2 or maximum 3 masters although other courses from other masters may seem interesting.

(3) Make use of the possibility to try classes the first to weeks of the semester and choose your classes based on academic interest and the people in these classes. Nice fellow students go for a great opportunity to make new relations.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of the opportunities present themselves in WhattsApp groups and all students are part of them and for the most part very willing to include Erasmus students in them.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange has been the academic opportunities. The learning experience and the new connections i have made stem from choosing great courses, which lead to great people which lead to a great stay. That combined with the ful immersion in the spanish language.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing commitments in Denmark with opportunities in Madrid while being away.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
